newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: Belgrade bourse quiet in dull holiday week.
newsitem.headline: Belgrade bourse quiet in dull holiday week.

text.p: The Belgrade Stock Exchange (BSE) reported on Monday a 4.352 million dinar ($765,092) turnover in a quiet holiday week ending May 2.
This compares to an average four to six million dollar turnover when the bourse works the whole week.
Last week, the BSE did not work for three days because of a long Orthodox Easter weekend and a two-day May 1 Labour day holiday.
"It was a dull holiday week, without any dramatic developments. With only two working days, most companies and banks were closed for the whole week," a trader said.
For the week ending May 2, the BSE reported the following details:
* Commercial paper accounted for 16 transactions worth 2.034 million dinars.
* Treasury bills traded eight times for a volume of 2.164 million dinars.

* The central bank sold a further 0.154 million dinars worth of bonds from its portfolio. Bonds, issued by the Serbian Commodity Reserve Agency, were sold on the secondary market. -- Gordana Filipovic, Belgrade newsroom, +381 11 222 4254
